clue.text: Charter cats to be trained for pest controllers ?

indicators.note: letters that are to be trained are drilled into a new order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hires out cats, once drilled, as an answer to vermin problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be trained' rearranges CHARTER and CATS together; the question mark admits that cats really are rat catchers.
explanation.definitionFit: People or animals employed to kill rodents are vermin exterminators.

clue.text: Protection a goatskin could provide for a god?

definitions.text: a goatskin could provide for a god

explanation.surface: A shield made of goat hide might keep a deity safe.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus and Athena carried a shield or cloak of goatskin, the original of the word that now means sponsorship or shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is patronage or shelter under someone's authority; the second is the goatskin shield borne by Zeus or Athena in myth.

clue.text: Vehicle off to the plant

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
off, as in gone off, means absent or away

explanation.surface: Someone drives off to the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory you might drive to, but it is the herb whose seeds flavour bread.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an umbelliferous herb grown for its aromatic seeds, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Race to keep fit — this pill needed

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside, so the race letters go round the word for fit

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
fit, as in fit for work, means able

explanation.surface: An athlete is told that staying in shape for a race requires medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A compressed medicinal dose is a pill, synonym-style.

clue.text: He's about to adjust the balancers

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters of He's go round the word for adjust

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to adjust is to alter

explanation.surface: A man is about to tune the balancing weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal; halteres are the tiny balancing organs behind a fly's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: In flies these are the small knobbed organs, modified hind wings, that stabilise flight like gyroscopes.

clue.text: To use up left-overs, cold starter with celery soup

indicators.note: a soup is a mixture, so the letters are stirred into a new order
the starter of a word is its opening letter, here from cold

explanation.surface: A cook makes a cold celery soup to use leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' and 'soup' suggest a menu; 'starter' takes the C of cold and 'soup' rearranges it with CELERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reusing discarded material or scraps instead of wasting them is reprocessing for further use.

clue.text: Great on visits, when working?

indicators.note: working means operating in a new way, so the three words are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: Someone excels at calling on people while on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when working' rearranges GREAT ON VISITS; the whole clue also describes detectives, whose work is calling on witnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives and inquirers are known for calling on people to question them as part of their job.

clue.text: Foreign soldier with relative about to arrive shortly, in the fort

indicators.note: about means around, so the soldier's letters go round the short form of arrive

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, foreign from a British setter's point of view
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrive
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: An overseas soldier and a family member are due to arrive soon at the fort.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the troops stationed somewhere, the word can mean the fortified post they occupy.

clue.text: Process to gee up dreary shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone wants a procedure to liven up a dull photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as a photo, fitting the surface about photography, but it is the anagram signal on TO GEE UP DREARY.
explanation.definitionFit: This early photographic method used silvered copper plates, so it is a photographic process.

clue.text: About to trap retrograde foreign banker

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to gin is to snare game in a gin trap

explanation.surface: Someone is about to ensnare a backward overseas financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword code for a river, something with banks; the reversed RE+GIN names an African river.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African river has banks, and lies abroad, so it is a foreign river in crossword terms.

clue.text: A battle helmet no protection against shrapnel

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear offers no defence against flying metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crimean War battle of 1854 gave its name to the knitted woollen hood soldiers wore there.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is the Crimean War engagement of 1854; the second is a knitted woollen hood that would stop no shell fragment.

clue.text: Not at home — otherwise we grab her!

parts.note: otherwise means else, as in 'or else'

indicators.note: to grab is to hold in your grip, so the letters of we enclose the word her

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kidnapper says she is out, or else they would seize her.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not at home is somewhere other than here, in another place.

clue.text: Four hundred odd Greeks here?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Roughly four hundred Greek people live somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four hundred odd' reads as an approximate count, but 'odd' rearranges FOUR with C; the question mark signals a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeks live on this Ionian island, which is part of Greece.

clue.text: Drew first two yellow patterns on cloth by this method

definitions.text: patterns on cloth by this method

parts.note: drew, as in a drawn game, means tied

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word yellow are taken

explanation.surface: Someone sketched two yellow designs on fabric using a certain technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' reads as sketching, but it is the sporting sense, a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: This technique patterns fabric by knotting or binding parts before dipping in colour.

clue.text: Dignified French maid, rising, took precedence

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid
to take precedence is to go first, so led

explanation.surface: A French maid stood up and claimed the right to go first.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised to the nobility, or given honour and grandeur, is exalted.

clue.text: He's backing bishop over severe changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A man supports the bishop despite harsh alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as supporting, but it means driving backwards; 'changes' rearranges RR and SEVERE together.
explanation.definitionFit: One who backs is a person going into reverse, an agent noun from the verb.

clue.text: Sorry, firm direction to pedestrian is needed

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
N, north, is a compass direction
pedestrian in the sense of dull or commonplace means trite

explanation.surface: A firm instruction to a walker is that an apology is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective for dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remorseful or penitent is feeling regret.

clue.text: Pack of wild dogs pursue beast, showing concentration of strength

parts.note: a gang is a pack or band, here of roaming dogs
a lion is a wild beast

explanation.surface: A pack of feral dogs chases a big cat, showing their combined power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentration of strength' is a figurative sense: a nerve centre, a hub of energy or activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a cluster of nerve cells, the word figuratively means a centre of force or activity.

clue.text: Could be paroled though dangerous when free

indicators.note: could be means might turn into, so the letters can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A prisoner might win release despite being a menace at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges PAROLED; 'paroled' and 'free' set a prison scene, but the big cat is dangerous when uncaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted big cat is a predator that poses a threat if it escapes.

clue.text: Crouch to toll bell in church

indicators.note: in places the bell-tolling word inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to toll a bell is to ring it

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to sound the bell inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower or shrink back in fear is to crouch.

clue.text: is hostile to sister's remedy

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a sibling's cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' reads as a noun, a sister's cure, but works as the verb to fix, rearranging SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing or fighting against something is withstanding it.

clue.text: Stop at entrance — you get licence inside

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the run of words stop at entrance

explanation.surface: A door attendant halts you while you obtain a permit indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An official grant giving exclusive rights to an invention is a licence of sorts.

clue.text: Ban also includes Jack

indicators.note: includes means the word for also holds the sailor inside it

parts.note: too means also
jack is slang for a sailor, as is AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: A prohibition also covers a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, but it is a sailor, abbreviated AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A social prohibition or forbidden subject is a ban.

clue.text: Passing a couple of poles to one in river

indicators.note: in places the letters for a, the poles and one inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
N and S are the north and south poles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone passes a pair of poles to a person standing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The TRENT is a river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-lived or fleeting is passing in the sense of temporary.

clue.text: Scoffed at, even outside

indicators.note: the poetic word for even goes outside the word at

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked even when out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed at' reads as mocked, but 'Scoffed' alone is the definition, gobbled; 'even' is the poetic E'EN, as in 'e'en so'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff, informally, is to gobble food greedily, so scoffed food has been consumed.

clue.text: Troops take chopper back to pit and continue the probe

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are army troops

indicators.note: back means the word for chopper is read in reverse

parts.note: an axe is a chopper
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry an axe back to a coal pit to carry on an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter for troops, but it is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect again or resume questioning is to carry on investigating.

clue.text: Is put about, made to beg like a dog

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog is pushed around until it is trained to beg.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog begging sits back on its haunches with front paws raised.

clue.text: Disastrous ratings dive? Publicity needed!

indicators.note: disastrous means ruinous, so the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A TV show's ratings plummet and it needs promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' reads as viewing figures, but its letters join DIVE as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting goods or services through paid notices is publicity.
